outcome: Topological features (network integration, segregation, clustering, global efficiency, small-world topology, small world indices, economy, modularity, average path length, degree distribution)
cohort: The participants were 110 fetuses from whom resting state MRI data sets were collected.
finding: The study found that neural circuitry underpinning the brain's ability to segregate and integrate information exists as early as the late 2nd trimester of pregnancy, exhibits small-world topology, and reorganizes with advancing gestational age.
